Encounter-rate weight per species x zone, from the occurrence rule's counts

Source: R/encounter_weight.R
encounter_weight.Rd

w = min(1, rate_zone / rate_reference), where rate_zone = the species' record rate in the zone (occupied / searched 0.5-degree blocks, occurrence_rule()'s rate) and rate_reference = its rate over the baseline (occurrence_rule()'s p_core: the other zones of the set, or the whole range). The weight is a MULTIPLIER on the merged value inside the zone. The tiers Tim White asked for apply in this order:

  • dropped (the gate): w = 0 – zero detections under adequate effort are a gate, not a weight; the rows are also in the exclusion table, so the weight is redundant there by design.

  • an override (protected, narrow range) or unsearched: w = 1 – unsampled is unknown, not rare; critical habitat is never downweighted.

  • no reference (p_core is 0 or NA: the species has no record anywhere else): w = 1 (the pooled fallback – nothing to compare against, so nothing is taken away).

  • otherwise w = max(floor, min(1, rate / p_core)); a zone at or above its reference rate is never UPweighted (cap at 1).

Usage

encounter_weight(x, floor = 0)

Arguments

x

a data frame as occurrence_rule() returns: rate, p_core, verdict, override (and mdl_key, zone_key, carried through).

floor

numeric in 0, 1; the smallest weight a kept zone can take (default 0: the rate ratio as measured).

Value

x with a w column (numeric in floor, 1, 0 where dropped) and w_reason (dropped | override | unsearched | no reference | rate ratio | at reference).

Examples

x <- data.frame(mdl_key = "a", zone_key = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
                rate = c(0.1, 0.5, 0, 0.02), p_core = c(0.4, 0.4, 0.4, 0.4),
                verdict = c("kept", "kept", "unsearched", "dropped"), override = NA)
encounter_weight(x)$w   # 0.25, 1, 1, 0
#> [1] 0.25 1.00 1.00 0.00
